baseline: Original heap, 16x7, slice8; exact frozen binaries from mesh/road transfer study.
training: Two existing tune sources; per-layout/source warmup, two randomized timed repeats. Top two plus baseline get three new repeats; select by geometric mean of source medians of confirmation only.
heldout: Four test sources never used for selection; each arm/source warmup plus three repeats. Selected layout vs 16x7 baseline, duplicate 16x7 control, and fixed training-selected Wasp, interleaved.
affinity: Worker CPU lists are rank*(span/ranks)+[0,ppn). Startup remains unbound as in baseline. Every runtime PE binding is verified. span128 spreads rank starts; span64/32 packs into one socket/two NUMA domains. A single rank uses contiguous cores. Each process region leaves >=1 core unused.
allocation: One exclusive 128-core Delta cpu-interactive node; fewer active workers do not release cores for another job.
prediction: Fewer active workers may reduce loaded rounds and contention on thin road frontiers; fixed-worker-count comparisons distinguish changing process count. Compact versus spread separates locality/resource reach. No guaranteed gain.
acceptance: All full independent digests, old scheduler, effective layout and affinity; diagnostic ledgers conserve work. Timing gain >=5% beyond duplicate-control variation is promising, then require separate-allocation confirmation before changing recommendation.
followup: Independently test chunk partial publication and distance-band width at fixed 16x7, then combine a promising queue with the training-selected layout. Preserve solver defaults.
